title: Default Mutable Argument
code:
def append_to(val, lst=[]):
    lst.append(val)
    return lst

print(append_to(1))
print(append_to(2))

bugs.explanation: The default `[]` is created once when the function is defined. All calls that omit `lst` share the same list. Use `None` as the default and create a new list inside: `if lst is None: lst = []`.

title: Passing by Reference vs Value

def zero_first(lst):

nums = [5, 10, 15]

title: Recursive Fibonacci
Function Shadowing Built-in
code:
def max(a, b):
    return a if a > b else b

print(max(3, 7))
print(max([1, 2, 3]))

bugs.explanation: Naming a function `max` shadows the built-in `max`. Later code that calls the built-in `max([1, 2, 3])` will call your two-argument function instead, raising `TypeError`. Use a different name to avoid shadowing.

title: Inner Function (Closure)
Positional After Keyword

bugs.explanation: Positional arguments cannot follow keyword arguments. This raises `SyntaxError`. Either put positional before keyword (`greet('Hi', 'Alice')`) or make all arguments keyword: `greet(greeting='Hi', name='Alice')`.

title: Nonlocal for Nested Scope
code:
def counter():
    count = 0
    def increment():
        nonlocal count
        count += 1
    increment()
    increment()
    return count

print(counter())

title: Recursion Limit
code:
import sys

def deep(n):
    if n == 0: return
    deep(n - 1)

sys.setrecursionlimit(500)
deep(1000)

bugs.explanation: The recursion limit is set to 500 but `deep(1000)` tries 1000 recursive calls — exceeding the limit and raising `RecursionError`. Call with a value within the limit (e.g. `deep(400)`).
